cutoff_convention: Publicly available before 2026-09-02 00:00:00 UTC; check exact version and statement.

binding.algorithm: SHA-256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON (sort_keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False)
binding.scope: The classes and knowledge documents only. Excludes policy and this audit to avoid a circular freeze hash.

launch_policy.candidate_questions: Freeze the ordered pairs absent from the baseline closure. Mark them as candidates with historical review pending; runs may start against this version.
launch_policy.baseline_trust: Accept cited pre-cutoff mathematical results as reviewed literature inputs. Do not require Lean formalization of existing proofs.
launch_policy.positive_score_gate: Before awarding each newly resolved pair, check the exact semantics, proof validity, pre-cutoff literature and implicit consequences of pre-cutoff results. Bind the dated eligibility decision to the exact pair and frozen dataset.
launch_policy.review_multiplicity: Review every pair for which points are sought, including pairs obtained only through closure. One discovery can have many points, but it does not bypass their historical eligibility checks.
launch_policy.zero_score_gate: An actual recorded model run may receive an official zero after the run is reviewed and every submitted proof candidate has been adjudicated. No historical openness certification of unclaimed pairs is needed to record that zero.
launch_policy.retrospective_omission: If a pre-cutoff theorem or its consequence was missed, the pair earns zero. Record the source and date, issue a correction, and recompute affected scores against the corrected eligibility mask while retaining the original run and freeze for provenance.
launch_policy.after_cutoff_results: Apply the run policy to attribution and publicly known post-cutoff proofs. Do not silently add them to the pre-cutoff baseline.
launch_policy.public_labels: Use recorded model/run identities. Keep the historical baseline row distinct from measured AI rows. Label hypothetical closure scenarios separately.
launch_policy.negative_search_policy: No-result searches and this AI audit never automatically mark a pair certified open.
launch_policy.independence: Require an exact statement about ZFC provability and non-provability plus its explicit metatheory. It does not enter ordinary inclusion/noninclusion closure.

limitations: AI-assisted review by a collaborating Codex agent. No human expert has certified all unknown pairs, and this file is not such a certification.
All 2,500 pairs are indexed; 100 ordered family groups have a semantic/closure screen. This is not 2,500 independent literature searches.
A conservative closure may omit known theorems or known conditional implications. The discovered Theta2P omission demonstrates why absence is only candidate status.
Recent searches are selective, not an exhaustive scan of every preprint, proceedings volume, journal, language, or unpublished proof before the cutoff.

Publisher/author metadata dates public evidence. Repository deposit and web-crawl dates do not establish original theorem dates. Sources with year-only dates remain coarsely dated; all such imported historical years precede 2026.
Some rechecks used primary abstracts rather than full proofs. These access limits are attached to the source records. Preprint claims are not validated merely because a dated abstract exists.
The benchmark uses total languages; promise, oracle, communication and query statements require a separately proved transfer before they can settle a pair.
The baseline theorems are literature-backed trusted inputs. This audit does not require, supply, or claim Lean proofs of them.

Lean operational definitions and the scorer do not by themselves prove equivalence with every textbook machine convention. New proof review must check that the submitted statement uses the frozen intended semantics.
Zero historical-baseline points is a convention. It does not establish the performance of any current AI system, nor the absence of post-cutoff public advances.

sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.title: On the Power of Probabilistic Polynomial Time: P^NP[log] ⊆ PP
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.locator: University of Rochester technical report TR275, February 1989, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.3
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.notes: Beigel, Hemachandra, and Wechsung. Original report date is February 1989; later repository deposit dates do not date the theorem.
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.inspection: Original report text, title page, Theorem 2.1 / Corollary 2.3, and original publication date; repository deposit date distinguished.

sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.title: A Simple Proof of Toda’s Theorem
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.locator: Theory of Computing 5, pp. 135–140; Theorems 3.1 and 3.3, Lemma 3.4
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.notes: Primary author proof. Theorem 3.3 states NP ⊆ BPP implies PH ⊆ BPP. Theorem 3.1 gives a randomized formula list preserving unsatisfiability and isolating a solution with high probability.
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.inspection: Publisher date and full-text Theorems 3.1 and 3.3; formula-list proof used for the parity specialization.

sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.title: Generalized Lowness and Highness and Probabilistic Complexity Classes
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.locator: Mathematical Systems Theory 22, pp. 37–46; author-hosted abstract, final sentence
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.notes: Recovers the Boppana–Håstad–Zachos result coNP ⊆ BP·NP implies PH ⊆ BP·NP. Here BP·NP is AM; it is not the oracle class BPP^NP. The author abstract, not a full-text proof, was rechecked in the September 2026 audit.
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.inspection: Primary author-hosted abstract with exact conditional statement; full paper proof not rechecked.

sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.title: If NP has polynomial-size circuits, then MA = AM
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.locator: Theoretical Computer Science 137(2), pp. 279–282; main theorem and publisher abstract
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.notes: Arvind, Köbler, Schöning, Schuler. DOI 10.1016/0304-3975(95)91133-B. Publisher abstract and author publication list were checked; full publisher PDF was not accessible during this audit.
sources_rechecked_in_this_pass.inspection: Publisher abstract and author publication list; full publisher PDF was inaccessible.
